analysis.title: Delta-One Flows & Positioning: Record Semis Inflows With Pivot to Unlevered; Munis/Mid-Term USTs Bid, Utilities/Money Market/Gold Sold; CTAs De-Risk US/Japan/Brazil
key_insights: Semiconductor ETFs took in a record ~$12.7Bn last week (4.3z; SOXX +$6.5Bn, SOXL +$2.8Bn, SMH +$2.6Bn), above the prior $9.3Bn record from late July. It was the second straight week led by semis, with a pivot toward unlevered products.
Outside semis, equity ETF sector flows were broadly weak: Utilities (-2.4z), Materials (-1.4z), Financials (-1.1z) and Staples (-1z). Technology took in $13.19Bn (3.5z).
Asset class ETF flows: Equities $23.4Bn (-0.2z), Fixed Income $15.2Bn (0.6z), Commodities -$1.6Bn (-0.9z), Currency/Multi-asset roughly flat.

Fixed income ETFs: Munis took in $4.4Bn (1.8z), a 4th straight week of strong but decelerating inflows. Medium-term government bonds took in $2.8Bn (2.1z) and Corporates 0.7z. Money Market (-$0.9Bn, -1.1z) and Loans (-1.2z) saw outflows.

Cross-asset hedges were pared back. Precious Metals ETFs saw -$1.6Bn (-0.9z), concentrated in GLD (-$2.3Bn), and Liquid Alts had their first weekly outflows in about 3 months (-1.5z), mainly managed futures products.

Regionally, US ETF inflows were near average ($17Bn, -0.1z). International DM was below average ($5.4Bn, -0.5z) with moderate Europe outflows (-0.5z) but strong Canada inflows (1.4z). Brazil flows were near flat after two weeks of strong inflows ahead of the final-round election.
Levered ETFs took in ~$4.3Bn (1.7z), led by SOXL (+$2.8Bn, its 2nd highest ever but well below last week's +$7.2Bn), TQQQ (+$1.3Bn) and SOXS (+$0.8Bn).
Style flows: Defined outcome ETFs drew strong inflows ($0.9Bn, 1.3z), while Multi-factor (-1.4z), Volatility (-0.8z) and Thematic (-0.7z) saw outflows.
Futures flows: large net buying (>1.5z) in S&P 500, FTSE 100, FTSE Taiwan, TAIEX, UST Long Bond, UK 10y and Copper. Large net selling (<-1.5z) in Dow Jones, SMI, China A50, NIFTY and CAD futures.

CTAs likely sold US equities as short-term signals turned negative on SPX/NDX and volatility rose, and likely sold Japan equities. They are near neutral across APAC overall while still short China, and sold Bovespa/BRL in this morning's sell-off.
In rates, CTAs likely trimmed shorts as short-term momentum turned positive in the US and Europe. They flipped short US Natgas, remain short metals ex-Copper, and are long USD vs DM FX ex-JPY.
CFTC: Asset Managers added to EAFE (1.5z) and cut VIX shorts (2.1z) w/w, likely following the Oct 16 intraday VIX spike. They extended duration, rotating out of UST 2y-10y into Ultra Bond futures.
CFTC: Leveraged funds significantly cut RTY shorts (+3z), sold VIX (-1.9z) and increased Ultra Bond shorts (-2.9z). Managed Money sold Copper (-1.9z), US Natgas and Ags.
Commodity moves over the week: Brent +6.2%, TTF +7.2%, US Natural Gas -15.3%, Gold -4.0%, Silver -5.9%. CTAs are long Brent, WTI, heating oil, gasoil and TTF, and short Gold and Silver.

Top performing ETFs last week were cybersecurity and cloud funds (WCBR +12.7%, BUG +12.6%, WCLD +11.8%). Worst were gold and silver miners (SGDJ -12.3%) and crypto-linked funds over four weeks (WGMI -37.2%).
Largest 1w ETF outflows: QQQ -$6.5Bn (-1.8z), SPY -$5.2Bn, GLD -$2.3Bn, IWM -$1.8Bn, XLF -$1.6Bn. Largest 1w inflows: SOXX $6.5Bn, VOO $6.2Bn, SOXL $2.8Bn, SMH $2.6Bn, MUB $1.6Bn.

sector_views.rationale: Record ETF inflows of ~$12.7Bn (4.3z) for the second straight week, rotating toward unlevered products. This is a flow observation, not a bank rating.
Largest sector ETF outflow at -$901Mn (-2.4z). This is a flow observation, not a bank rating.
ETF outflows of -$1,457Mn (-1.1z), with XLF among the largest fund outflows. This is a flow observation, not a bank rating.

crypto_views: Bitcoin futures: 1w net flow -0.2z, 1w return -0.8%, CTA signal neutral. Ether futures: 1w net flow -0.3z, CTA neutral.
Crypto ETFs: Cryptocurrency products had net 1w flow of $71Mn (0.0z) and 4w flow of -$1,778Mn (-0.7z).
Crypto-linked ETFs were among the worst 4-week performers (WGMI -37.2%, STCE -28.4%, BKCH -28.0%, ZCSH -26.5%).
BTC1 current level is 79,655, with CTA signal long. Prior week CTA signal was neutral.
risk_factors: Volatility picked up, turning short-term CTA signals negative on SPX/NDX.
Brazil assets face additional pressure from CTA selling in this morning's sell-off.
Semis flow concentration: the record inflow follows a record-sized SOXL inflow the prior week (+$7.2Bn).
vol_and_positioning: CTAs likely sold US equities as short-term signals turned negative on SPX/NDX and volatility rose.
The VIX had an intraday spike on Oct 16. Asset Managers cut VIX shorts (2.1z) and Leveraged funds sold VIX (-1.9z) w/w.
VIX futures CTA signal is neutral at 19.10, vs 17.68 on the 1-month momentum level. Prior week's signal was neutral.
Leveraged funds cut RTY shorts significantly (+3z). CTAs remain short RTY.
Dealers were net short S&P 500 futures at -636,931 contracts (1.0z). Asset managers were long 901,377 (-1.1z), down 14,458 w/w.
Volatility ETFs saw outflows (-0.8z). Defined outcome ETFs drew inflows (1.3z).
geopolitical: Brazil's final-round runoff election: ETF flows were quiet in the last week, and CTAs sold Bovespa/BRL in this morning's sell-off.
